title: Usage of UV-curable oligomer-based adhesive agent in hermatypic coral experimental research
author: Takeuchi, Yamashiro, et al.

steps.title: Gather equipment and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all items listed in Table 1: plastic seawater tank (65 × 110 × 18 cm), diagonal cutting pliers (110 mm MP4‑110 and 150 mm FPN‑150FS, Fujiya), 250 mm 318‑8 stainless steel forceps (K‑18‑250, Kowa), UV‑curable adhesive Bondic® with its UV‑LED light, sterilized filter paper (Kimwipes®), polycarbonate hexagon head bolts (PCBT‑0510, Wilco), UV‑cut glass (YX‑540, Yamamoto Kogaku), disposable gloves (8‑4053‑01/02/03, As One), mesh substrate components – thermoplastic fluoropolymer screen (mesh 2.14 mm, F‑3056‑008, Flon), ethylene‑vinyl acetate screen (mesh 7.5 mm, N‑523, DAIPLA), plastic square tube, 18‑8 stainless steel forceps for weight, cable ties – and for transport: triple‑layer plastic bag (0.1 mm), portable cooler (30 L, Daiwa Light Trunk SU 3000RJ), crushed ice (1–2 kg), digital thermometer (O‑209BL), and temperature logger (Tidbit v2).

steps.title: Relocate donor coral
steps.instruction: Transfer donor colonies of Acropora digitifera or A. tenuis from the large aquarium (77 × 168 × 36 cm) with running seawater to a shallow experimental tank (65 × 110 × 18 cm) also supplied with running seawater.

steps.title: Cut coral fragments
steps.instruction: Using either size of diagonal cutting pliers (110 mm MP4‑110 or 150 mm FPN‑150FS), cut the tip of each branch‑like part to a length of approximately 1.0–1.5 cm, making a clean cut to minimise damage.

steps.title: Store cut fragments
steps.instruction: Place the freshly cut coral fragments back into the shallow holding aquarium (65 × 110 × 18 cm) and keep them submerged until the attachment procedure.

steps.title: Prepare fragment surface
steps.instruction: With the 250 mm 318‑8 stainless steel forceps, remove a fragment from the holding tank and gently blot the cut surface with sterilized filter paper to absorb moisture.

steps.title: Apply Bondic and attach to bolt
steps.instruction: In a shaded area or indoor room, dispense a small drop of Bondic® onto the dried cut surface and immediately press the fragment onto the top of a polycarbonate hexagon head bolt (PCBT‑0510).

steps.title: Cure adhesive with UV light
steps.instruction: Activate the UV‑LED light supplied with Bondic® and irradiate the bonded area for approximately 5–10 seconds, ensuring complete polymerisation.

steps.title: Hold attached fragment in shallow tank
steps.instruction: Return the bolt with the attached coral fragment to the shallow aquarium to keep it wet until the mesh substrate is prepared.

steps.title: Assemble mesh substrate and insert bolt
steps.instruction: Layer the thermoplastic fluoropolymer screen (mesh 2.14 mm) over the ethylene‑vinyl acetate screen (mesh 7.5 mm); fix the two screens together on plastic square tubes with small cable ties and place 18‑8 stainless steel forceps inside the tubes for weight. Widen the openings of the top screen as needed, then screw each polycarbonate bolt with its coral fragment into the mesh.

steps.title: Install substrate in larger aquarium
steps.instruction: Transfer the assembled mesh substrate with attached bolts into a larger aquarium supplied with continuous running seawater.

steps.title: Transport substrate to distant lab
steps.instruction: Three days after attachment, place the substrate in a triple‑layer plastic bag (0.1 mm) containing about 14 L of seawater; seal the bag and put it inside a 30 L portable cooler with 1–2 kg of crushed ice on top. Monitor the internal temperature with a digital thermometer and a Tidbit v2 logger, keeping it below 28 °C. Transport the cooler from Sesoko Station to Ehime University (≈930 km) – total travel time about 7 h, including 2 h of aerial flight.

steps.title: Acclimate fragments to new salinity
steps.instruction: At the destination, measure the seawater salinity in the bag and increase it by 1 psu per hour over 2–3 hours to match the laboratory seawater conditions.

steps.title: Place substrate in rearing aquarium
steps.instruction: After acclimation, move the mesh substrate (with its top fluoropolymer screen) into a small 72 L aquarium placed inside an incubator, following the rearing method of Hirayama et al. (size adjusted).

steps.title: Reattach any detached fragments
steps.instruction: Five days after transport, identify any fragments that detached from bolts and re‑attach them using the same Bondic® application, UV curing, and shaded‑area procedure described earlier.
